content.inline:
# Trust monitors

A trust monitor answers one question — *may this subject perform this action on this object?* — and returns `true` or `false`. Anywhere an actor decides who may do what, the answer should come from a monitor, so the rule is reusable, replaceable and reviewable.

## The check

`(@convex.trust/trusted? monitor subject action object)` — omitted action and object are `nil`. The subject is almost always `*caller*`; the action a short literal keyword (`:mint`, `:update`); the object an address or id. Inside an actor:

```clojure
(when-not (@convex.trust/trusted? minter *caller* :mint)
  (fail :TRUST "No rights to mint"))
```

A monitor reference is an account address, optionally scoped (`[#78 1467476]` — the same actor, a different rule). A bare address trusts only itself, so "the owner" needs nothing deployed. `nil` denies everything: the safe default.

## Compose, do not write

`convex.trust.monitors` provides monitors that need no deployment: `permit-subjects`, `permit-actions`, `all`, `any`, `everyone`, `before`/`after`/`between` (a time window), `rule` (a predicate), `owns` (holds an asset), `delegate` (deny first, then allow, else a base monitor — the order you want for revocation).

```clojure
(@convex.trust.monitors/all
  (@convex.trust.monitors/permit-subjects #13 #17)
  (@convex.trust.monitors/permit-actions :open :close))
```

Let whoever controls a resource choose its rule: take a monitor as configuration (as a token's `:minter`) rather than baking a list of addresses into an actor.

## Writing one

Implement `check-trusted?` as a callable of exactly three arguments returning a strict boolean. No side effects (it runs inside `query`), O(1) work with a small constant, and never a scan of arbitrary data — a monitor runs on every check, so an expensive one is a denial-of-service vector.

## Fail closed

A checker treats any error or non-`true` result as denial and never lets an error propagate. From protocol version 1 `trusted?` does this itself (query-wrapped, errors caught, result coerced); on a network still at genesis, wrap caller-supplied monitors yourself. Keep action keywords literal at the call site — an action taken from untrusted input lets the caller choose which rule they are checked against.

Specification: CAD022 (`trustmon`). Related libraries: `convex.trust.whitelist`, `convex.trust.ownership-monitor`, `convex.trust.delegate`, `convex.trust.governance`.
